The Communion of the Apostles

Eucharistic Communion of the Apostles · Communion with Bread

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

1Corinthians11:23–26

Matthew 26:26–29

King James Version · Scripture previews

The selected fifteenth-century panel is catalogued as the Eucharist with bread. It belongs to the Trinity Cathedral iconostasis at Sergiev Posad.

What is depicted

Christ gives Communion to approaching apostles beside an altar-like table. This is the bread-communion panel, distinct from its wine companion and from the narrative Last Supper around a dining table. The source attributes it to the Daniel Chorny and St. Andrey Rublev workshop.

History and tradition

For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:

And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

[2] 1Cor 11:23–24

Published explanation

After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.

Paul’s published account of the Eucharistic words; the image’s ritual composition is not presented as an eyewitness photograph of the Last Supper.

[2] 1Cor 11:25–26

And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

The corresponding Gospel wording, quoted separately from Paul’s account.

[2] Matthew 26:26
